recipes.title: Traeger Pork Shoulder Carnitas
recipes.yield: About 1.8kg cooked, shredded (6 to 8 servings with freezer portions)
recipes.timing: 45 min active / 10 to 12 hr total (smoke + rest)
recipes.equipment: Traeger pellet grill, instant-read thermometer, digital scale, butcher paper or foil, cast iron pan
method: Combine 27g kosher salt, 10g black pepper, 15g ancho chile powder, 8g cumin, 6g oregano, 10g granulated garlic, 8g granulated onion, and 6g smoked paprika. Coat the 2700g pork shoulder evenly and let it dry brine uncovered in the fridge at least 8 hours, ideally overnight.
Set the Traeger to 225°F. Place the pork shoulder fat-cap up and smoke until the internal temperature reaches 165°F, roughly 6 hours.
Pull the shoulder and wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil with 240g orange juice, 60g lime juice, 240g chicken stock, and 3 bay leaves poured in before sealing.
Return to the smoker at 225°F and cook until probe-tender and the internal temp reads 203°F, another 3 to 4 hours. The probe should slide in with almost no resistance.
Rest wrapped for 45 minutes. Shred the meat, discarding excess fat cap, and reserve any rendered fat and braising juices.

To crisp: heat a cast iron pan hard with 60g reserved rendered fat (or lard). Add shredded pork in a single layer and let it sit undisturbed 3 to 4 minutes until the edges caramelize and crisp before tossing.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste and adjust salt after crisping, the reduction concentrates flavor. Splash in a little reserved braising liquid if it needs moisture back.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with corn tortillas (naturally GF), charred tomato-guajillo salsa roja, diced onion, and cilantro.
recipes.storage: Portion into freezer bags with a little braising liquid, up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of stock, then crisp again in a hot dry pan.
recipes.chefNote: Expect a long stall around 160°F to 165°F. Normal, and not a sign the smoker is failing.

recipes.title: Charred Tomato-Guajillo Salsa Roja
recipes.equipment: Comal or cast iron pan, blender
method: Char the 500g tomatoes, 100g onion, and 15g garlic (skins on) on a comal or dry cast iron preheated to roughly 500°F surface temperature (a drop of water should skitter and vanish in under 2 seconds), turning occasionally, until blackened in spots, about 8 to 10 minutes. Peel the garlic once cool enough to handle.
While the vegetables char, toast the 30g guajillo and 8g pasilla chiles in a dry pan over medium heat, 20 to 30 seconds per side, until fragrant and pliable.
Submerge the toasted chiles in 120g hot stock and soak 15 minutes until fully softened.
Blend the charred tomatoes, onion, garlic, softened chiles, and their soaking liquid with 6g salt and 10g vinegar until smooth.

Heat 15g avocado oil in a saucepan until shimmering. Pour in the blended salsa carefully (it will spatter) and fry, stirring, 5 to 7 minutes until it darkens slightly and the raw chile smell cooks off.
Taste and adjust salt.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Balance heat and acid last, add extra vinegar in small 5g increments if it tastes flat.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve warm or at room temp alongside carnitas, tacos, or eggs.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 week in an airtight container, or freeze up to 2 months.
recipes.chefNote: Dried chiles burn in seconds and scorched chile turns the whole batch bitter.

recipes.title: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs
recipes.equipment: Dutch oven, oven
method: Season the 1800g short ribs on all sides with 18g kosher salt and 5g black pepper. Let sit at room temp 30 minutes.
Heat 30g avocado oil in a Dutch oven over high heat until nearly smoking. Sear the ribs on all sides, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deeply browned. Remove and set aside.
Lower heat to medium. Add 200g carrots, 150g celery, and 200g onion to the fat in the pot; sweat 8 to 10 minutes until softened. Add 20g garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in 60g tomato paste and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it darkens and coats the pan.
Deglaze with 500g red wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer until reduced by half, about 8 minutes.
Return the ribs to the pot and add 500g beef stock, 0.4g bay leaves, and 4g thyme sprigs. Liquid should come two-thirds up the ribs. Bring to a simmer, cover, and transfer to a 300°F oven.

Braise 3 to 3.5 hours, until the meat reads 203 to 207°F internal at the thickest point and a probe slides in with no resistance. Below 195°F the collagen hasn't rendered and the meat will be tough no matter how long it looked done.
Rest ribs in the liquid 15 minutes, then remove. Skim excess fat from the braising liquid, reduce over medium-high heat to a sauce consistency, and stir in 15g balsamic vinegar to finish.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the reduced sauce before serving, add salt in small pinches, and a touch more balsamic if it needs brightness.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over mashed potatoes, polenta, or GF pasta, ribs napped generously with sauce.
recipes.storage: Cool completely, then portion with sauce into freezer containers up to 3 months. Reheat covered at 325°F until warmed through, or gently on the stovetop.
recipes.chefNote: Below 195°F the collagen has not rendered and the ribs stay tough no matter how done they look. Reduce the braising liquid hard at the end; it should coat a spoon.

recipes.title: Khao Soi-style Northern Thai Chicken Curry
recipes.equipment: Dutch oven or wide pot

items.note: bell pepper in the paste is fine, it cooks into the curry
about 2 limes; start here, adjust at the end

method: In a Dutch oven over medium heat, bloom 60g red curry paste and 10g curry powder in the thick cream skimmed from the top of the 800g coconut milk, stirring 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the 900g chicken thighs and 60g shallots, 15g garlic; turn to coat in the paste and sear lightly, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and 240g chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover partially, and cook 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken reaches at least 165°F internal and is tender.
Remove chicken, shred or leave on the bone as preferred, and return to the pot.
Season with 30g fish sauce and 20g palm sugar; simmer 5 more minutes to let the sugar dissolve. Finish with lime juice to taste.
Cook 400g rice noodles separately according to package directions. Ladle broth and chicken over noodles.
Garnish with cilantro, sliced shallot, and chile oil.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Balance fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime last, it should taste salty, a little sweet, and bright, not flat.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with extra lime wedges and pickled mustard greens if available.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate broth (without noodles) up to 4 days, or freeze up to 2 months. Cook noodles fresh when reheating.
recipes.chefNote: Bloom the curry paste in the thick cream skimmed off the top of the coconut milk until the oil separates. That split is the flavor base.

recipes.title: Summer Shrimp Salad with Toasted Shrimp-Shell Oil
recipes.equipment: Instant-read thermometer, digital scale, fine-mesh strainer

items.note: less dressing/more finish salt if spring mix; more dressing if arugula
halved, salted and drained if no feta
thin sliced, ice-water soaked (longer soak + smaller qty for red onion)
optional; if used, skip salting the tomatoes
2g in the dressing, 1g flaky at the finish

prep: Salt and drain the 200g halved cherry tomatoes 15 minutes if not using feta, to firm the flesh and prevent the plate from weeping; skip or reduce this step if feta is going in.
Soak 40g sliced onion in ice water 15 minutes for red onion, 5 minutes for shallot.
method: Peel the 400g shrimp, reserving shells. Pat shrimp dry and refrigerate until ready to cook.

Toast the reserved shells in 80g avocado oil over low heat, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oil turns red-orange and smells toasty. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing the shells to extract all the oil; discard solids.
Whisk the warm shell oil with 30g lime juice, 15g rice vinegar, 5g fish sauce, and 5g honey. Season with salt to taste.
Sear the shrimp over high heat in a thin film of shell oil, 60 to 90 seconds per side, pulling at 120°F internal. Look for a loose C, not a tight O.
Toss the greens with two-thirds of the dressing, then top with drained tomatoes, drained onion, shrimp, and 60g feta if using. Drizzle with the remaining shell-oil dressing.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Finish with a pinch of flaky salt on the shrimp just before serving.
recipes.servingNotes: Best served immediately while the shrimp are still warm against the cold greens.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; does not hold or freeze well. Shell oil alone keeps refrigerated up to 1 week.
recipes.chefNote: Shrimp carry over to about 130°F off the heat; past 145°F they turn rubbery. Red onion needs a longer soak and smaller quantity than shallot. Spring mix needs less dressing and more finish seasoning than arugula.

recipes.title: Hawaiian-Style Chili (Zippy's Copycat)
recipes.yield: About 2.3kg finished chili (6 to 8 servings over rice, with freezer portions)
recipes.equipment: Large pot or Dutch oven, food processor (optional, for prepping sausage and veg), potato masher
recipes.chefNote: Adapted from mypinterventures.com. Poblano stands in for the original bell pepper as a flavor choice, since it cooks in fully either way. Ground spices scorch in under a minute at this heat. The mayonnaise at the end rounds out the acidity and does not read as mayo.

items.item: Portuguese sausage, casing removed, finely chopped

items.note: bell pepper works here too, it cooks in fully

items.item: Chili beans in mild chili sauce, undrained

items.note: 5g kosher salt + 1g black pepper to start
stirred in off heat, right before serving

prep: Remove the casing from the 283g Portuguese sausage and pulse in a food processor to hamburger-sized bits, or chop finely by hand.
Finely dice 100g celery, 160g onion, and 50g poblano. Thinly slice 85g bacon.
method: In a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, brown the 454g ground beef, breaking it up with a potato masher until no large chunks remain and it reads 160°F internal. Drain excess fat and return the pot to the heat.

Add the 283g chopped Portuguese sausage and 85g sliced bacon. Cook just until both are heated through and the bacon has rendered some fat, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain if there's a heavy pool of oil; a little left behind will flavor the vegetables.
Add 100g celery, 160g onion, and 50g poblano to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion turns translucent, 5 to 6 minutes.
Lower heat to medium. Stir in 16g chili powder, 1g cumin, 0.5g oregano, and 1.4g paprika. Toast until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the 454g chili beans (undrained), 439g kidney beans (undrained), 454g tomato sauce, 3g powdered chicken stock, 120 to 240g water, 1 bay leaf, 2 to 4g brown sugar, 15g Worcestershire sauce, 30g ketchup or chili sauce, and 5g red wine vinegar if using. Stir to combine.

Bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Lower heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered another 20 minutes, until slightly thickened. Season with 5g kosher salt and 1g black pepper.
Off the heat, right before serving, stir in 28g to 42g mayonnaise.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Adjust salt, brown sugar, and vinegar to taste before the mayo goes in, the mayo mellows sharp edges, so get the base seasoned first.
recipes.servingNotes: Ladle over steamed white rice, Zippy's-style. Good with shredded cheese, chopped green onion, or a few dashes of hot sauce.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. If freezing, hold back the mayonnaise and stir it in fresh after reheating, it can separate if frozen in.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.equipment: Large skillet or Dutch oven, potato masher, 9x13 baking dish, oven
recipes.chefNote: Lamb makes it shepherd's pie; the beef version is a cottage pie. Both work. Mash by hand or ricer, never a mixer: overworking releases starch and turns the mash gluey, and Yukon Gold gets there faster than Russet, so Gold also takes less milk. The egg yolk gives the top its glossy, deep-brown finish. Seal the potato to the edges or the gravy bubbles up through the cracks, and rest 10 minutes or the filling runs when cut.

items.item: Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
items.note: Gold potatoes: reduce milk to about 90g, added gradually
Russet amount, use less for Gold, see chef's note
1 yolk, for a browned glossy top

items.item: Cornstarch or GF all-purpose flour blend

items.note: 6g kosher salt + 1g black pepper for the filling

prep: Boil the 1350g potato chunks in well-salted water until a knife slides in with no resistance, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain well and return to the hot pot for a minute to steam off excess moisture.

Mash 1350g potatoes with 85g butter, 8g kosher salt, and 1g white pepper by hand or ricer. Add warm milk gradually, up to 120g for Russet or about 90g for Yukon Gold, stopping once smooth. Cool slightly, then beat in 18g egg yolk. Set aside.
method: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Heat 15g avocado oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high. Add the 900g ground lamb and brown, breaking it into small pieces, 6 to 8 minutes, until it reads 160°F internal. Drain excess fat, leaving a thin film behind.
Add 160g onion, 150g carrots, and 100g celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 7 minutes. Add 12g garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in 30g tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until it darkens. Sprinkle in 20g cornstarch and stir to coat everything evenly, cooking 1 minute to lose the raw starch taste.

Pour in 350g stock and 15g Worcestershire, scraping up any browned bits. Add 2g thyme sprigs, 2g minced rosemary, and 0.2g bay leaf. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, 8 to 10 minutes, until the gravy has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in 90g frozen peas, then season with 6g kosher salt and 1g black pepper. Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Transfer the filling to a 9x13 baking dish and spread into an even layer.
Dollop the mashed potato over the filling and spread to the edges, sealing the gravy in completely. Drag a fork over the surface to create ridges.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the filling is bubbling at the edges and the potato top is golden brown. For deeper color, broil the last 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the gravy before topping with potato, it should taste rich and a little savory-sweet from the Worcestershire; add salt in small pinches, it concentrates further as it bakes.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve straight from the baking dish, scooped so each portion gets filling and topping together.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze (baked or unbaked) up to 3 months. Reheat covered at 350°F until the center is hot, uncovering the last 10 minutes to re-crisp the top.

recipes.title: 3-2-1 Traeger Baby Back Ribs
recipes.timing: 20 min active / 7 hr total (smoke + braise + glaze)
recipes.equipment: Traeger pellet grill, instant-read thermometer, digital scale, foil boats
recipes.chefNote: Promoted from your Traeger.com import. The longer end of the smoke window gives a deeper smoke ring. Steam off the foil is intense. The glaze is mostly sugar and goes from set to burnt in under a minute at 400°F.

items.item: Baby back pork ribs, membrane removed

prep: Remove the membrane from the back of both racks by sliding a butter knife under it at one end and pulling it off in one piece with a paper towel for grip.
Whisk 60g yellow mustard, 60g Dijon, a splash of the 120g apple juice, and 15g Worcestershire into a wet rub.
method: Set the Traeger to 180°F. Coat both racks evenly with the mustard mixture, then season with 30g pork rub across both racks, all sides.
Place ribs bone-side down directly on the grate and smoke at 180°F for 3 to 3.5 hours.
Raise the Traeger to 225°F. Lay each rack in a foil boat, top with 110g brown sugar and 115g warmed honey, and pour in the remaining 90g apple juice as braising liquid. Seal the foil tightly.
Braise at 225°F for 2 to 2.5 hours, until a bone twists loose with gentle pressure and the meat has pulled back about 1cm from the bone ends.
Open the foil carefully, brush the ribs with the reduced braising liquid, and place meat-side down on the grate at 400°F for 2 to 5 minutes to set the glaze.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If the glaze tastes flat after the high-heat finish, brush with a little more reduced braising liquid before slicing.
recipes.servingNotes: Slice between the bones and serve with extra warmed glaze on the side.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat wrapped in foil with a splash of apple juice at 300°F until warmed through.

recipes.title: Basil-Crusted Rack of Lamb with Glazed Carrots, New Potatoes & Mint Yogurt
recipes.equipment: 2 cast iron pans, food processor, instant-read thermometer
recipes.chefNote: Promoted from MasterClass (Gordon Ramsay). GF panko in place of regular. The second coat of Dijon is the glue that holds the crust through slicing.

items.item: Racks of lamb, frenched, fat cap removed

items.note: 8g kosher salt + 1g black pepper for 900g lamb
1 lemon, zest all of it, juice yields about 45g
start here, then adjust with lemon

prep: Pulse 20g basil, 15g parsley, 225g GF panko, 18g salt, and 50g Parmesan in a food processor until bright green and evenly fine. Taste and add more salt or Parmesan if needed.
Bring lamb to room temperature and season all sides with 8g kosher salt and 1g black pepper, pressing the racks into the seasoning to coat evenly.
method: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Heat 15g grapeseed oil in each of 2 cast iron pans over medium-high until just smoking. Sear the lamb racks bone-side up, using the bones as a handle, 60 seconds per side until browned all over.

Add 4 crushed garlic cloves, the thyme bunch, and 28g butter to the pans; baste for 1 minute, pushing the toasted aromatics behind the racks. Transfer pans to the oven and roast 4 to 5 minutes, until the lamb reads 125°F internal for rare (pull earlier for rarer, it will carry over about 5°F while resting).
Rest the racks bone-side down on a tray. Brush the flesh side with 60g Dijon, let it tack up 2 minutes, then brush a second coat. Press the basil crust onto the mustard, packing it between the bones.

Meanwhile, blanch 250g carrots in well-salted boiling water 2 minutes, shock in an ice bath. In a sauté pan, melt 40g honey with the star anise and cinnamon sticks over medium heat; add the blanched carrots and toss 3 minutes, then add 40g butter and 60g stock, cooking 2 to 3 minutes until glazed and the liquid evaporates.

Boil 400g potatoes in salted water 10 minutes until a paring knife slides in easily. Drain, cool 10 minutes, halve, and sear cut-side down in 15g olive oil 3 to 5 minutes until browned; flip, add 28g butter, season with 3g kosher salt and 1g black pepper, and baste 3 more minutes.
Stir 10g chiffonade mint into 200g yogurt with lemon zest and juice to taste; season with 2g kosher salt.
Slice each rack between the ribs into individual chops. Plate with the yogurt sauce, carrots, potatoes, and a final pinch of flaky salt over the lamb.
recipes.finalSeasoning: The mint yogurt sauce should be bright and cool against the rich crust, add lemon juice in small amounts if it tastes flat, salt if it tastes dull.
recipes.servingNotes: A special-occasion plate, spoon yogurt sauce first, shingle the lamb chops over it, arrange vegetables alongside.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Leftover lamb keeps refrigerated 2 days; reheat gently to avoid overcooking past medium-rare.

recipes.title: Traeger Carne Asada
recipes.equipment: Traeger pellet grill, instant-read thermometer
recipes.chefNote: Hold the marinade to 2 hours. Past that the citrus firms the surface texture.
prep: Whisk together the marinade: 200g orange juice, 80g lemon juice, 60g lime juice, 12g garlic, 20g cilantro, 20g minced jalapeño, 3g cumin, 55g olive oil, 6g salt, and 1g pepper until the salt dissolves.
method: Trim silverskin from the 900g skirt steak. Place in a resealable bag with the marinade, coating all over. Marinate in the fridge 2 hours.
Remove steak, discard marinade, pat dry, and season both sides with 25g prime rib rub. Rest at room temperature 30 minutes.
Set the Traeger to 225°F and preheat with the lid closed 15 minutes. Place the steak directly on the grates and smoke 45 minutes.
Pull the steak, raise the Traeger to 450 to 500°F, and preheat 15 minutes with the lid closed.
Return the steak to the grill and sear about 2 minutes per side, until internal temp reads 135°F for medium-rare.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste a slice before serving, a squeeze of fresh lime brightens it if the char reads heavy.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with warm corn tortillas, salsa, and lime wedges.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate sliced leftovers up to 3 days. Reheat briefly in a hot pan, skirt steak toughens fast if overcooked on the reheat.

recipes.title: Carnitas (Family Stovetop Version)
recipes.equipment: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

items.item: Pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

items.note: to barely cover; top up if it drops below the pork

prep: Toss the 1360g pork chunks with 18g salt, 2g pepper, and 7g cumin, coating evenly.
method: Heat 110g lard in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Sear the seasoned pork on all sides until deeply browned, about 10 minutes total, working in batches if crowded.

Add 150g quartered onion, 8g garlic, 0.2g bay leaf, 2.5g cinnamon stick, 60g orange juice, 60g lime juice, and the squeezed orange halves. Pour in about 700g water to barely cover the pork, adding 60g milk if using.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook 2 to 2.5 hours, until the pork reads 200 to 205°F internal and shreds easily with a fork.
Uncover, raise heat to medium-high, and reduce the liquid until nearly gone, turning the pork occasionally to keep it from sticking.
Once the liquid has mostly evaporated, let the pork fry in its own rendered fat until crispy and caramelized at the edges, 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to crisp new surfaces.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste after crisping and adjust salt, the long reduction concentrates flavor fast.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with corn tortillas, diced onion, cilantro, and salsa.
recipes.storage: Portion into freezer bags up to 3 months. Reheat in a hot dry pan to re-crisp.
recipes.chefNote: Sear in batches. A crowded pot steams instead of browning.

recipes.title: Carnitas (Dr. P.'s Slow Cooker Version)
recipes.equipment: Slow cooker or Dutch oven set to low
recipes.chefNote: Root beer or Dr. Pepper both work. Undercooked pork will not crisp at the finish, so hit 200°F to 205°F before shredding.
method: Layer into the slow cooker in this order: 2040g frozen pork shoulder, then 200g quartered onion and 18g smashed garlic, then 15g kosher salt, 4g black pepper, 4g ground cumin, 2g dried oregano, 5g chili powder, 2g paprika, and 15g brown sugar. Pour in 355g root beer and 240g stock, then 80g fresh orange juice with the spent halves tucked alongside, and 0.4g bay leaves.

Cover and cook on low 5 to 6 hours. By hour 2 the pork should be fully thawed, by hour 4 it starts turning tender, and by hour 5 to 6 it shreds easily. Probe the thickest point: you want 200 to 205°F internal, and the probe should slide in with no resistance.
If it resists shredding or reads under 200°F, give it another 30 to 45 minutes.
Shred the pork in the braising liquid, then spread on a sheet pan and broil 3 to 5 minutes for crisp edges, or crisp in a hot cast iron pan with a ladle of braising liquid and 15g lard.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the shredded pork in its juices before crisping, add a pinch of salt if the braising liquid's sweetness is dominating.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with corn tortillas, pickled onion, and your salsa roja.
recipes.storage: Portion into freezer bags with a little braising liquid, up to 3 months. Reheat gently, then crisp in a hot dry pan.

recipes.title: Chicken and Paneer with Turmeric Rice
recipes.equipment: Cast iron pan, Dutch oven for rice

items.note: 6g kosher salt + 1g black pepper, split between chicken and paneer
6g kosher salt + 1g black pepper, split between chicken and paneer

prep: Combine the 680g chicken thighs with half the lemon juice, 3g oregano, 1g coriander, 9g garlic, 3g kosher salt, 0.5g black pepper, and 55g olive oil; let marinate while you prep everything else.
method: Get a cast iron pan smoking hot over high heat. Sear the marinated chicken 2 minutes per side to develop color, then remove, dice into bite-size chunks, and set aside.

Return the pan to high heat until smoking again, add a film of oil, and add the diced chicken back in. Cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy with brown bits stuck to the pan, about 4 to 5 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F internal. Deglaze with the remaining lemon juice, scraping up the brown bits to coat the chicken.

Toss the 454g paneer with 1g oregano, 0.5g coriander, 3g kosher salt, 0.5g black pepper, and 14g olive oil. Pan-fry over medium heat, turning occasionally, until golden brown on most sides, about 6 to 8 minutes.

For the rice: heat 28g olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium, add 1g turmeric and 0.5g cumin, and toast until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add 380g rice and stir to coat, toasting 4 to 6 minutes until the grains smell nutty. Add 400g broth and 400g water, season with salt, and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce to a bare simmer, and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Remove from heat and rest, covered, 15 more minutes.
Whisk 110g mayonnaise, 115g yogurt, 30g vinegar, and 5g lemon juice for the white sauce.
Fluff the rice and serve topped with chicken, paneer, and a drizzle of white sauce.
recipes.finalSeasoning: The white sauce should taste tangy, not flat, add vinegar in small splashes if needed.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve family-style over the turmeric rice with white sauce on the side.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 4 days. Reheat chicken and paneer in a hot pan to re-crisp; rice reheats well with a splash of water, covered.
recipes.chefNote: Get the pan genuinely smoking before the chicken goes in. Paneer browns better dry, so pat it before it hits the oil.

recipes.title: Chicken Biryani (Josh's Version)
recipes.timing: 45 min active / 2.5 to 4.5 hr total (includes marinating)
recipes.equipment: Large heavy pot with tight-fitting lid, aluminum foil
prep: Combine the 900g chicken with 20g garlic, 10g ginger, 6g coriander, 2g cayenne, 1g turmeric, 1g garam masala, 245g yogurt, and 12g of the salt. Stir until well coated and marinate in the fridge 2 to 4 hours.
Rinse the 380g rice, cover with water in a bowl, and soak 30 minutes.
method: Heat 150g oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high, then lower to medium. Add the 450g sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, 12 to 15 minutes until soft and touched with golden brown. Remove onions with a slotted spoon, reserving half the oil in the pot and setting the rest aside.

Bring 1900g water to a boil in a separate large pot with the remaining 6g salt. Drain the soaked rice and boil vigorously 4 to 6 minutes, until the grains are no longer brittle but still firm to the bite. Drain immediately.

In the pot with the reserved oil, layer half the marinated chicken, then half the par-cooked rice, half the fried onions, and half the cilantro. Repeat with the remaining chicken, rice, onions, and cilantro. Sprinkle 30g water over the top and drizzle with the reserved oil.
Seal the pot with foil under the lid. Bake at 375°F for 60 minutes without lifting the lid. Chicken should read 165°F internal and the rice should be tender.
Uncover carefully (steam will rush out) and fold the layers together gently before serving so the rice doesn't turn mushy.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the rice at the edges before serving, if underseasoned, toss with a little extra salt dissolved in warm water rather than dry salt, so it distributes evenly.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve hot, straight from the pot, with raita or a simple cucumber salad alongside.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat covered with a splash of water at 325°F, or in the microwave with a damp paper towel over the dish.
recipes.chefNote: Par-boil the rice to about 70 percent so it finishes in the oven without going to mush.

recipes.title: Crispy Panko Chicken Breasts
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, meat mallet or rolling pin
recipes.chefNote: Even thickness is the whole recipe: a full breast burns its crust long before the center comes up. Carryover takes it from 160°F to 165°F. Rest on a rack, since paper towel steams the crust soft.

items.item: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts, pounded to 1.5cm even thickness

method: Pound 454g chicken breasts between parchment to an even 1.5cm thickness, or halve horizontally into cutlets.
Beat 50g egg in a shallow bowl. In a second shallow bowl, combine 90g GF panko, 1.5g garlic powder, 1.5g onion powder, 3g fine sea salt, and 0.5g black pepper.

Dip each cutlet in the 50g beaten egg to coat, then press into the 90g panko mixture on both sides until fully coated. Rest the breaded cutlets on a rack 10 minutes so the coating sets and won't slough in the pan.

Heat 55g corn oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers and a panko crumb sizzles on contact, about 350°F. Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and the internal temperature reads 160°F.
Rest on a wire rack 5 minutes.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If the crust browns before the chicken is through, finish in a 375°F oven 4 to 5 minutes rather than pushing the stovetop heat higher and burning the panko.
recipes.servingNotes: Slice and serve over greens, or whole with a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a 375°F oven on a rack to keep the crust crisp, the microwave will make it soggy.

recipes.title: Miso Glazed Salmon
recipes.timing: 10 min active / 1 to 3 hr total (includes marinating)
recipes.equipment: Large skillet or sheet pan, instant-read thermometer
recipes.chefNote: The salt in miso acts as a cure. Past 3 hours the flesh starts to firm.
prep: Season the 900g salmon fillets with 3g kosher salt and 1g black pepper.
Whisk 70g miso, 30g tamari, 14g brown sugar, 15g rice vinegar, and 5g sesame oil until smooth. Reserve 15g of this marinade for glazing later.
method: Coat the salmon in the remaining marinade and refrigerate 1 to 3 hours.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Place salmon in a skillet or on a sheet pan, discarding the used marinade. Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish is almost opaque through.
Brush with the reserved 15g glaze and broil on high 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, until the surface caramelizes and the center reads 125 to 130°F.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If the glaze tastes one-note sweet, a few drops of extra rice vinegar right before serving brings it back into balance.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over rice with a side of quick-pickled cucumber.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days; reheat gently to avoid pushing past medium.

recipes.title: Nashville Hot Chicken Tenders
recipes.timing: 45 min active / 3 to 5 hr total (includes brining)
recipes.equipment: Deep heavy pot or skillet, instant-read thermometer, fine-mesh strainer
recipes.chefNote: The original serves over white bread; use GF bread or a corn tortilla. Longer brining than 2 hours turns the texture spongy.

items.note: 8 to 10 tenders, this is the only chicken in the recipe
enough for about 5cm depth in the pot

prep: Combine the lemons, 2400g cold water, 120g salt, 100g sugar, bay leaf, garlic, and 3g pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve, and cook 5 minutes. Strain, discard solids, and stir in the 4700g ice water to cool the brine.
Once cool, stir in 300g buttermilk and 140g pickle juice. Add 900g chicken tenders and brine no more than 2 hours.
method: Whisk 310g GF flour blend, 25g cornstarch, 18g salt, 7g paprika, 4g cayenne, 2g pepper, 1.5g garlic powder, and 9g onion powder in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk 480g buttermilk with 75g hot sauce.

Remove chicken from the brine and pat dry. Dip each piece into the flour mixture, then the buttermilk mixture, then back into the flour, pressing to coat thoroughly. Let coated chicken rest on a rack 15 to 20 minutes until the coating sets and looks slightly dry.
Add 1800g neutral oil to a heavy pot, about 5cm depth, and heat to 350°F. A pinch of the flour mixture should sizzle and turn golden within a few seconds.
Fry 3 to 4 tenders at a time, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and internal temp reads 165°F. Don't crowd the pot. Drain on a rack.
Whisk 240g of the hot frying oil with 45g cayenne, 20g brown sugar, 3g chili powder, 3g garlic powder, and 3g smoked paprika until blended. Brush generously over the hot fried chicken immediately.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the hot oil coating before brushing, if it's too sharp, whisk in a touch more brown sugar; if it's flat, more cayenne.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over GF bread or in corn tortillas with dill pickles and coleslaw.
recipes.storage: Best fresh and hot. Leftover fried chicken loses crispness; reheat in a 400°F oven on a rack, never the microwave.

recipes.title: Tangy Spiced Chicken
recipes.timing: 10 min active / overnight marinate + grill time
recipes.equipment: Grill or griddle

items.note: 7g kosher salt + 1g black pepper for 900g chicken

prep: Whisk 28g olive oil, 9g garlic, 2g cumin, 2g smoked paprika, 2g sweet paprika, 1g cayenne, 1g coriander, 1g cinnamon, 1g turmeric, 21g honey, 15g lemon juice, 30g yogurt, 7g kosher salt, and 1g black pepper into a marinade.
method: Coat the 900g chicken in the marinade and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours, for the spices to fully penetrate.
Bring chicken to room temperature 20 minutes. Grill or griddle over medium-high, turning once, to 165°F internal, about 6 to 7 minutes per side for thighs and less for breasts.
Right before serving, squeeze the remaining 15g lemon juice over the hot chicken.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If it tastes flat off the grill, it needs that final fresh lemon hit, not more salt.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve with rice or a simple salad and extra lemon wedges.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan to avoid drying out.
recipes.chefNote: The final raw lemon is what makes this tangy rather than just spiced, and it cannot be added earlier.

recipes.title: Madison's Favorite Beef Tacos
recipes.yield: 8 servings (2 nights for a family of 4)
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, slow cooker or Instant Pot
recipes.chefNote: The original uses minced red bell pepper. It cooks fully into the filling, so bell works; poblano is kept for depth.

items.note: bell pepper works here too, it cooks in fully

method: Brown the 900g beef in a large nonstick skillet over high heat, breaking it into small pieces as it cooks, about 5 minutes, until it reads 160°F internal with no pink remaining.

When no longer pink, add 4g of the 7g cumin along with 10g kosher salt, 10g chili powder, 5g paprika, 1g oregano, 70g onion, 40g poblano, and 6g garlic. Stir and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables soften.

Transfer to a slow cooker with 120g water, 0.2g bay leaf, and 240g tomato sauce. Cover and cook on high 3 hours or low 6 to 8 hours. (For a stovetop version, simmer covered 25 to 30 minutes instead.) Discard the bay leaf and stir in the remaining 3g cumin.
Warm the taco shells according to package directions. Fill each with about 30g beef, then top with 11g shredded romaine, 7g shredded cheddar, and 9g diced plum tomato.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the beef before filling shells, it should taste well-seasoned on its own since the toppings are mild.
recipes.servingNotes: Makes enough for two taco nights. Set up toppings buffet-style.
recipes.storage: Freeze the beef filling (without shells/toppings) up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight, reheat on the stove or microwave.

recipes.title: Mississippi Pot Roast
recipes.equipment: Cast iron pan, slow cooker or Instant Pot
recipes.chefNote: If you would rather not use packets, build it from ranch seasoning plus beef bouillon and a cornstarch slurry.
prep: Trim the chuck roast of excess exterior fat, leaving enough for flavor. Pat dry and season with 7g kosher salt and 1g black pepper.
method: Heat 15g avocado oil in a cast iron pan over high heat until shimmering. Sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 3 to 4 minutes per side, rendering out some of the surface fat.
Place the seared roast in the slow cooker. Sprinkle the top with 14g ranch mix and 28g au jus mix, arrange the 5 pepperoncini and 56g butter on top.
Add 450g carrots, 10 potatoes, 150g onion, and 120g water around the roast.
Cover and cook on high 4 hours, or pressure cook on high 25 minutes with natural release, until the roast reads 203°F internal and shreds easily with two forks.
Shred the roast in its juices and toss the vegetables to coat.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste the braising liquid before serving, it's usually well-seasoned from the mixes, but add salt if it tastes thin.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over mashed potatoes, rice, or GF noodles with plenty of the braising liquid spooned over.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of the reserved liquid.

recipes.title: Chicken Wild Rice Soup
recipes.equipment: Large pot
method: Heat 28g olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the 454g chicken and cook until browned on all sides, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add 150g onion, 120g carrots, and 100g celery. Cook until starting to soften, about 5 minutes. Add 12g garlic and cook 1 more minute.
Stir in 160g wild rice, 1g thyme, 1g rosemary, and 0.2g bay leaf; toast 1 minute.
Add 1900g chicken broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 40 to 50 minutes, until the wild rice kernels have split open and are tender.
Return the chicken to the pot and cook 10 to 15 more minutes, until it reaches 165°F internal. Season with 7g kosher salt and 1g black pepper, remove the bay leaf, and garnish with parsley.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Wild rice soaks up salt as it sits, taste again just before serving and adjust.
recipes.servingNotes: A full meal on its own; good with GF crusty bread.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop, thinning with a splash of broth if it's thickened.
recipes.chefNote: Wild rice keeps absorbing salt as it sits, so season again just before serving.

recipes.title: Ginger Miso Soup with Soba & Turnips
recipes.equipment: Medium pot
recipes.chefNote: Use 100 percent buckwheat soba; most blended sobas contain wheat. Boiling kombu turns the broth bitter and slick, so hold it at a bare simmer.

items.item: 100% buckwheat soba or rice noodles, cooked

items.note: start here, adjust at the end

prep: Rinse the kombu piece gently under cold water.
method: Simmer 5g kombu in 950g water 10 minutes at a bare simmer, not a boil. Remove the kombu once softened, then bring the water to a full boil.
Reduce heat and add the remaining 240g water. In a small bowl, loosen 70g miso with some of the hot dashi until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.

Add 5g ginger, 25g scallions, 35g shiitakes, 240g quartered turnips, and 60g carrots. Simmer on low until the turnips are fork-tender, 35 to 40 minutes. If the soup thickens too much, thin with an extra cup or two of water.
Add 115g tofu and the cooked soba or rice noodles. Taste and season with tamari to taste.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Miso loses aroma if boiled hard after it's added, keep the heat gentle from this point on, and adjust saltiness with tamari rather than more miso.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve hot in deep bowls; add turnip greens at the very end if using, just to wilt.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 to 4 days. The noodles will keep absorbing broth, add extra water when reheating if it's gotten too thick.

recipes.title: Jamaican Beef Stew
recipes.equipment: Dutch oven, oven
recipes.chefNote: Habaneros go in whole and come out whole. Pierced or chopped, they take the stew somewhere much hotter.

items.note: 12g kosher salt + 1g black pepper for 1130g beef

prep: Adjust an oven rack to the lower-middle position and preheat to 300°F.
method: Heat 14g olive oil in a Dutch oven over high heat until smoking. Season the 1130g beef with 12g kosher salt and 1g black pepper, add to the pot, and cook without moving until well-browned on one side, about 6 minutes.

Stir to loosen the meat, then add 150g onion and 250g carrots. Cook, stirring, 2 minutes. Reduce heat to medium and add 16g whole habaneros, 8g garlic, and 55g rum. Bring to a boil and simmer 2 minutes.
Add 475g stock, 1g allspice, 0.5g cinnamon, 5g hot sauce, 4g thyme sprigs, 0.4g bay leaves, 4g brown sugar, 15g red wine vinegar, 411g tomatoes, 15g tamari, and 23g steak sauce. Stir to combine.
Return to a boil, cover, and transfer to the oven. Cook until the beef reads 203°F internal and is tear-apart tender when pierced with a fork, about 1.5 hours.
Discard 4g thyme sprigs, 0.4g bay leaves, and the 16g whole habaneros, leaving one in for more heat if wanted. Reduce on the stovetop if not thick enough. Season with kosher salt in 2g increments.
Garnish with scallions and serve over rice.
recipes.finalSeasoning: This stew should be sweet-hot-savory in balance, if it's flat, a touch more brown sugar and vinegar in equal small amounts usually fixes it faster than salt alone.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve hot over white rice, scallions scattered over the top.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop.

recipes.title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
recipes.equipment: Saucepan, shallow pot
recipes.chefNote: Well-fermented, sour kimchi makes this dish. Fresh kimchi will taste thin no matter how long it simmers.

items.item: Dried anchovies, heads and guts removed
Korean radish or daikon, thinly sliced
Pork shoulder or pork belly, sliced thin

prep: Combine the 20g dried anchovies, 50g radish, green onion roots, and dried kelp in a saucepan with 950g water. Boil 20 minutes over medium-high, then lower heat and simmer 5 more minutes. Strain and reserve 475g of the stock.
method: In a shallow pot, add the 454g kimchi and 60g kimchi brine. Add the 227g pork and 160g sliced onion.
Slice 30g of the 45g green onions on the diagonal and add to the pot. Add 5g salt, 8g sugar, 6g gochugaru, and 18g gochujang. Drizzle 5g sesame oil over the top and pour in the 475g anchovy stock.
Cover and cook over medium-high heat 10 minutes.
Uncover and stir the seasonings through with a spoon. Lay the 200g tofu over the top.
Cover and cook another 10 to 15 minutes over medium heat, until the 227g pork reads 160°F internal and the kimchi has softened.
Chop the remaining 15g green onion and scatter over the top. Remove from heat and serve immediately.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Well-fermented kimchi brings most of the sourness, if the stew tastes flat, a touch more gochujang deepens it; if it's too sharp, a pinch more sugar rounds it out.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve bubbling hot straight from the pot with a bowl of steamed rice and banchan.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days, the flavor deepens as it sits. Reheat on the stovetop, not the microwave, to keep the pork from toughening.

recipes.title: Polish Kielbasa & Cabbage Soup
recipes.equipment: Large soup pot or Dutch oven
recipes.chefNote: The vinegar and lemon cut the kielbasa's richness. Add more of either if the soup tastes heavy.

items.item: Green cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces

method: Heat 28g oil in a large soup pot over medium heat until shimmering, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the 340g kielbasa and brown 2 to 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add 100g celery and 120g carrots to the pot, season with 8g kosher salt and 1g black pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, 5 to 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in 1g rosemary, 2g smoked paprika, and 2g caraway seeds; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the kielbasa to the pot along with 0.4g bay leaves, 450g potatoes, 454g cabbage, 30g vinegar, and 1900g stock.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the cabbage is tender and the 450g potatoes read 205°F internal / pierce with no resistance.
Stir in 15g lemon juice if using, and adjust salt and pepper. Remove bay leaves before serving.
recipes.finalSeasoning: The vinegar and optional lemon are there to cut the richness of the kielbasa, add a little more of either if the soup tastes heavy.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve hot with GF rye bread if you can find it, or on its own.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop.

recipes.title: Chana Palak Masala
recipes.equipment: Large pan
method: Heat 40g oil in a large pan over medium-high. Sauté 160g onion until golden, about 6 to 8 minutes.

Add 12g garlic and 8g ginger, cook 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until the raw garlic smell is gone. Add 6g coriander, 2g turmeric, 3g cumin, and 1 to 2g cayenne; toast 2 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant.
Add 400g crushed tomatoes, 400g chickpeas, and 120g stock. Bring to a boil, then lower to medium-low and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 5g salt, 4g sugar, and 100g spinach. If the spinach is frozen, raise heat until bubbling again, then simmer 5 more minutes.
Stir in 2g garam masala, 22g lemon juice, and 75 to 150g coconut milk (more for a richer curry). Adjust salt if needed. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Balance heat, acid, and richness last, more cayenne for heat, more lemon for brightness, more coconut milk to mellow it out.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over basmati rice.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently, thinning with a splash of water or stock if needed.
recipes.chefNote: Bloom the whole spices in oil before the aromatics. Ground spices go in later so they do not scorch.

recipes.title: Coconut Chickpea Curry (Vegan & GF)
recipes.equipment: Deep pot
method: Heat 28g coconut oil in a deep pot over medium-high. Add 160g onion and 400g tomatoes, season with 5g sea salt and 1g black pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes release their juices and the onion softens, about 10 minutes.
Add 454g chickpeas, 9g garlic, 9g garam masala, 2g curry powder, and 0.5g cumin. Stir to combine.
Add 383g coconut milk and stir again. Whisk in 5g coconut flour if using, to thicken slightly. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer 10 to 12 minutes.
Off the heat, squeeze in 25g lime juice and stir. Taste and season with sea salt in 2g increments. Cool slightly before serving.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If it tastes flat, it almost always needs the lime, not more salt, taste again after the squeeze before adjusting further.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over rice with extra lime wedges.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
recipes.chefNote: The lime at the end lifts the dish. If it tastes flat, reach for lime before more salt.

recipes.title: Saag Paneer
recipes.equipment: Large nonstick pan, food processor or blender
recipes.chefNote: Squeeze the thawed spinach genuinely dry or the sauce will be watery. Reserve a third unblended for texture.

items.item: Small green chiles, seeded and chopped

items.note: mild, medium, or hot to taste

items.item: Frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

items.note: start here; frozen spinach needs more than you expect

method: Heat 5g of the 20g butter and 5g of the 20g oil over medium heat (about 325°F pan surface) in a large nonstick pan. Add the 454g paneer and fry until browned on two or more sides, 12 to 15 minutes, turning and shaking the pan occasionally. Remove and set aside.

Wipe out the pan. Heat the remaining 15g butter and 15g oil, then add 160g onion, 15g ginger, 9g garlic, and 15g chopped green chiles. Fry over medium heat until the onion is soft but not browned, about 5 minutes.
Add 5g curry powder and 2g cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add 6g salt and 570g spinach, stirring until well blended. Reserve a third of the spinach for a coarser texture, then transfer the rest to a blender with enough of the 355g yogurt to make it creamy.
Return the blended mixture to the pan, adding the reserved unblended spinach if using. Thin with warm water if needed.
Stir in the paneer, heating gently until it softens slightly. Top with cilantro if desired.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste after blending, the yogurt should read as creamy tang, not sour; add more only in small amounts, it's hard to walk back.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve over basmati rice or a GF flatbread.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, high heat can cause the yogurt to break.

recipes.title: Basic Pesto
recipes.equipment: Food processor
method: Combine 40g basil, 18g pine nuts, and 8g garlic in a food processor. Process until very finely minced.
With the machine running, slowly dribble in the 110g olive oil and process until smooth.
Add 50g Parmesan and process briefly, just long enough to combine.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste before storing, a pinch of salt if the Parmesan alone isn't carrying enough seasoning.
recipes.servingNotes: Toss with GF pasta, spread on GF toast, or spoon over grilled chicken or fish.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days with a film of olive oil on top to prevent browning, or freeze in ice cube portions up to 3 months.
recipes.chefNote: Over-processing the cheese turns the pesto pasty. Pulse it in at the very end.

recipes.title: Chimichurri
recipes.equipment: Knife or food processor

items.item: Fresno chili or jalapeño, finely diced, seeds removed for less heat

method: Finely dice 40g shallot, 20g fresno or jalapeño, and 14g garlic.
Combine with 115g red wine vinegar and 6g salt in a bowl; let sit 5 minutes so the vinegar softens the shallot's bite.
Stir in 20g cilantro, 20g parsley, and 5g oregano, then whisk in 165g olive oil until combined.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Let it sit 20 to 30 minutes before serving if you have time, the flavors round out and the raw shallot mellows.
recipes.servingNotes: Classic with grilled steak, but also good on roasted vegetables or chicken.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 week in an airtight container; bring to room temperature before serving so the olive oil re-liquefies.
recipes.chefNote: Let it sit 20 to 30 minutes before serving. The vinegar mellows the raw shallot and the flavors round out.

recipes.title: Roasted Green Hot Sauce
recipes.equipment: Sheet pan or comal, blender, fine-mesh strainer
method: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss 110g poblano, 80g jalapeños, 16g serranos, and 14g garlic (skin on) with 14g olive oil and 1g of the 5g salt. Roast on a sheet pan 15 to 20 minutes, until blistered and softened.
Meanwhile, boil the 160g quartered onion in water 5 to 8 minutes until translucent and soft. Drain.
Once cool enough to handle, peel the garlic. Stems can stay on the chiles if you want more heat carried through, or remove for a milder sauce.
Blend the roasted chiles, garlic, boiled onion, 20g cilantro, 25g lime juice, 2g cumin, and the remaining 4g salt until smooth.
Pass through a fine-mesh strainer for a smooth, pourable sauce; skip this step if you prefer it with more body.
recipes.finalSeasoning: To make it milder, remove the seeds and ribs from the jalapeños and serranos before roasting, or swap one serrano for another poblano.
recipes.servingNotes: A great all-purpose table sauce, eggs, tacos, grilled meats.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 weeks in a sealed jar, or freeze up to 3 months.
recipes.chefNote: Removing seeds and ribs from the jalapeños and serranos before roasting makes it milder, as does swapping a serrano for another poblano.

recipes.title: Smoked Baked Beans
recipes.equipment: Traeger or oven, large saucepan, 9x13 baking dish
recipes.chefNote: Poblano in place of the original bell pepper, a flavor choice rather than an avoidance.

items.item: Poblano pepper, cored, seeded, finely chopped

method: Preheat the Traeger (or oven) to 350°F. Spray a 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray.

In a large saucepan, brown the 454g ground beef and 283g kielbasa together over medium-high heat. When the beef is about halfway cooked, add 110g onion, 80g poblano, and 40g diced jalapeños. Continue cooking until the beef reaches 160°F internal and the vegetables have softened, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add all 5 cans of beans (undrained chicken broth included), 420g barbecue sauce, 300g ketchup, 75g mustard, 75g Worcestershire, 38g tamari, and 55g brown sugar. Simmer 5 minutes to combine.

Transfer to the prepared baking dish. Smoke (or bake) at 350°F for 1 hour, stirring every 15 to 20 minutes so the top doesn't dry out. Finished beans should read 190 to 200°F in the center and have visibly thickened at the edges.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste before serving, if it's too sweet from the barbecue sauce, a splash more Worcestershire balances it.
recipes.servingNotes: Great alongside smoked meats, this recipe scales easily for a crowd.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat covered at 325°F or on the stovetop.

recipes.title: Fried Rice
recipes.equipment: Large sauté pan or wok
recipes.chefNote: Day-old refrigerated rice is the difference between fried rice and a sticky clump. Fresh rice has too much surface moisture.

items.item: Cooked and chilled rice, short-grain preferred

method: Heat 7g butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high until melted. Add 100g whisked eggs and cook, stirring occasionally, until scrambled. Remove to a plate.
Add another 14g butter to the pan. Add 120g carrots, 110g onion, 65g peas, and 9g garlic; season with 3g kosher salt and 1g black pepper. Sauté about 5 minutes, until the onion and carrots soften.

Increase heat to high, add the remaining 21g butter and stir until melted. Immediately add the 640g rice, green onions, and 45g tamari, stirring until combined. Continue sautéing 3 minutes, letting the rice rest between stirs so it crisps on the bottom.
Add the scrambled egg back in and stir to combine. Remove from heat and stir in the sesame oil. Taste and add more tamari if needed.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Add tamari in small increments at the end, it's easy to oversalt fried rice since the rice itself has no seasoning to buffer against.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve immediately while the bottom is still crisp.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan, not the microwave, to bring back some of the crisp texture.

recipes.title: Japanese Cucumber Salad (Sunomono)
recipes.equipment: Colander
recipes.chefNote: Salting and squeezing the cucumber first is what keeps the dressing from turning watery on the plate.
prep: Thinly slice the cucumber by hand or with a food processor.
method: Rub the cucumber slices with 9g salt and drain in a colander 5 minutes. Rinse under cold water and squeeze tightly to remove excess liquid.
In a small bowl, mix 7g sugar, 10g tamari, and 30g rice vinegar until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the dressing with the cucumber, sprinkle with 3g sesame seeds, and mix well.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Should taste bright and lightly sweet-salty, thin with a touch more vinegar if it's too salty from the initial rub.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve cold as a side to grilled or glazed fish.
recipes.storage: Best within a few hours; the cucumbers release water and dilute the dressing if held overnight.

recipes.title: Mexican Rice
recipes.equipment: Large pot with lid
method: Heat 28g olive oil in a large pot over medium-low. Add 110g onion and the jalapeño; cook, stirring frequently, until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Raise heat to medium and add 30g tomato paste, 8g garlic, and 280g rice; cook, stirring frequently, about 3 minutes to toast the rice.
Add 800g chicken broth, 5g salt, 0.5g pepper, 1g chili powder, and 1g cumin. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until all the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Add 65g peas, 10g cilantro, and 10g lime juice; fluff with a fork. Let sit a few minutes to dry out before serving.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and lime last, the rice absorbs seasoning unevenly as it steams.
recipes.servingNotes: Classic side for any Mexican-style main.
recipes.storage: Freezes well up to 3 months in a flat layer in sealable bags. Reheat from frozen in the microwave with 1 to 2 tbsp water.
recipes.chefNote: Toast the rice in oil until it smells nutty and turns chalk-white before any liquid goes in.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Spinach Garlic Noodles
recipes.equipment: 2 skillets
recipes.chefNote: Give the mushrooms room and leave them alone until they release and reabsorb their liquid. Crowding steams them.

items.item: Sesame seeds and red chile flakes, for garnish

method: Heat 14g olive oil in a medium skillet. Add 6g garlic and cook 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant and just starting to color.
Add the 454g mushrooms and toss to combine. Add 15g water and 18g tamari, and cook over medium heat until the mushrooms shrink and release their liquid, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the 115g spinach in two additions, cooking until wilted and tender. Season with 3g kosher salt and 1g black pepper. Remove from heat and set aside.
Cook and drain the 283g GF noodles according to package instructions.

In a large skillet, heat 14g olive oil. Add 15g garlic and cook 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Reduce heat, add 45g tamari and 5g sesame oil, then fold in the mushroom-spinach mixture. Toss in the cooked noodles until coated in the sauce.
Serve warm, garnished with sesame seeds and chile flakes.
recipes.finalSeasoning: GF noodles can turn gummy if oversauced, add tamari gradually and toss well before adding more.
recipes.servingNotes: A full vegetarian side or light main.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; GF noodles don't reheat as well as wheat noodles. Refrigerate up to 2 days, reheat gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Family Potato Salad
recipes.equipment: Large pot, colander
recipes.chefNote: Cracking skins mean the potatoes are close. Salt again after chilling, since cold potato salad needs more than it seems to warm.

items.item: Kosher baby whole pickles, diced small

items.note: 10g kosher salt + 2g black pepper; salt again after chilling

prep: Boil 8 eggs to hard-cooked, cool, peel, and dice.
method: Boil 2270g whole potatoes 20 to 30 minutes, checking frequently after 20 minutes. Pull at 197°F to 200°F internal.
Strain and shock the potatoes in a cold water bath. Peel and dice once cool enough to handle. Any slightly underdone pieces can go in a bowl and microwave in 30-second intervals until tender.
In a large bowl, combine the diced potatoes with 400g diced egg, 180g diced pickles, 60g red onion, 55g mustard, 120g pickle juice, and 850g mayonnaise.
Season with 10g kosher salt and 2g black pepper, folding gently to avoid mashing the potatoes.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Taste after chilling, not right after mixing, cold potato salad needs more salt than it seems to right out of the bowl.
recipes.servingNotes: Best served chilled, at least 2 hours after mixing.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Does not freeze well, the mayo-based dressing separates.

recipes.title: Stovetop Wild Rice
recipes.equipment: Saucepan with lid
method: Combine 160g wild rice, 710g water or stock, and 3g salt in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer 40 to 45 minutes, until some kernels have burst open.
Drain any excess liquid, stir in 14g butter, and serve.
recipes.finalSeasoning: If cooking in water rather than stock, taste and add a bit more salt at the end, it needs more than you'd expect.
recipes.servingNotes: Good on its own or as a base for a grain bowl.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 6 months, drained, in airtight containers.
recipes.chefNote: Burst kernels are the doneness cue. Timing varies with the age of the rice.

recipes.title: Orange Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
recipes.equipment: Stand mixer, 2 9-inch round cake pans, wire racks
recipes.chefNote: 1:1 GF baking blend with xanthan gum (Bob's Red Mill or King Arthur Measure for Measure). GF batters go gummy if overmixed, so stop the moment the flour disappears. Beat the cream cheese completely smooth at the start, since lumps will not disperse later, and frost only once the cakes are fully cool.

items.note: 1 orange, zest all of it, 80g juice

prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. If toasting pecans and coconut, spread separately on sheet pans and toast pecans 6 to 8 minutes, coconut 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely. Cool and set aside.
Grease the bottoms of 2 9-inch round cake pans and line with parchment.
method: Whisk 350g GF flour blend, 10g baking soda, 5g cinnamon, 4g nutmeg, 1g ginger, and 1.5g salt in a medium bowl.
Cream 227g butter with 200g granulated sugar and 213g brown sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy, 3 to 4 minutes. Reduce to low and add 200g eggs one at a time.
Add 60g milk, then the flour mixture in roughly 90g increments, scraping the sides between additions and mixing just until incorporated.
Stir in 8g vanilla, the zest of 1 orange and 80g of its juice, and 55g coconut oil. Fold in the 320g shredded carrot by hand.
Divide batter evenly between the pans, smooth the tops, and bake at 350°F on the middle rack 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean (start checking at 30 minutes).
Cool in the pans 15 minutes, then turn out onto wire racks parchment-side up and cool completely before frosting.
Beat 227g cream cheese and 113g butter until completely smooth. Add 360g powdered sugar in three additions on low, then 7g orange liqueur, 2g vanilla, and 1g sea salt. Beat 1 minute until light.
recipes.finalSeasoning: For the frosting: beat 227g cream cheese and 113g butter with a dash of salt until smooth, add 7g liqueur/extract and 2g vanilla, then slowly beat in 360g powdered sugar until smooth. Chill 30 minutes before frosting.
recipes.servingNotes: Level the cake tops, frost between layers and on top/sides, and finish with toasted pecans and coconut.
recipes.storage: Store frosted cake refrigerated; best within a few days. Unfrosted layers freeze well wrapped tightly, up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Olive Oil Matcha Cake
recipes.equipment: 8-inch cake pan, stand or hand mixer

items.item: Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the pan
Powdered sugar, plus more for dusting

prep: Whisk 110g olive oil, 120g milk, and 18g poppy seeds together in a glass measuring cup; let sit 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease an 8-inch cake pan with olive oil and line the bottom with parchment.
method: Whisk 100g eggs and 6g vanilla into the oil mixture.
In a large bowl, whisk together 166g almond flour, 83g oat flour, 168g sugar, 11g matcha, 6g baking powder, and 3g salt.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and mix until just combined. Pour into the pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
Bake at 350°F for 45 to 55 minutes, until the cake springs back when poked and a toothpick comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack and flip right-side up to cool completely.
Whip 240g cold heavy cream to soft peaks that hold a slumping ridge. Serve alongside the cooled cake rather than frosting it.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Whip 240g cream with 30g powdered sugar and 4g vanilla to soft peaks while the cake cools.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve at room temperature with the soft-whipped cream on the side. The cake is better on day two once the almond flour hydrates fully.
recipes.storage: Keeps at room temperature in an airtight container 3 to 5 days, or freeze up to 1 month.
recipes.chefNote: Loose, soft-peak cream is the counterweight to the matcha's tannin. Stiff peaks read heavy here.

recipes.title: Halloween Chocolate Cutout Cookies
recipes.timing: 45 min active / 2 to 4 hr total (includes chilling)
recipes.equipment: Rolling pin, cookie cutters, piping bags
recipes.chefNote: 1:1 GF baking blend with xanthan gum. GF cutout dough softens fast, so work in batches and keep the rest chilled. Excess flour is what makes GF cutouts chalky, so cap any addition at 8g and chill instead.

items.item: 1:1 GF all-purpose flour blend, plus more for rolling
Royal icing or simple glaze icing

prep: Whisk 235g GF flour, 62g cocoa powder, 4g baking powder, and 0.5g salt together; set aside.
method: Beat 172g butter and 200g sugar on high speed until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes. Add 50g egg and 4g vanilla, beat 1 minute to combine, scraping the bowl as needed.
Add the dry ingredients and mix on low until combined. If the dough is too soft to roll, add up to 8g more GF flour.
Divide the dough in half. Roll each half between sheets of parchment dusted with cocoa powder to about 1/4-inch thick.
Stack the rolled doughs (still on their parchment) and chill 1 to 2 hours, up to 2 days.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Cut shapes from the chilled dough, re-chilling 10 minutes if it softens too much to transfer cleanly.

Arrange cookies 3 inches apart on parchment-lined sheets. Bake at 350°F for 11 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set. Cool on the sheet 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely before decorating.
Tint 300g royal icing in batches with 2g gel food coloring, keeping each bowl covered with a damp cloth so it doesn't crust over.

Outline each cooled cookie with stiff icing, let the border set 15 minutes, then flood the center with icing thinned to the consistency of honey. Dry completely at room temperature 6 to 8 hours before stacking.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Not applicable to a sweet dough, but taste-test one plain cookie before decorating a full batch to confirm sweetness balance.
recipes.servingNotes: Pipe icing borders, flood centers, and decorate as desired. Let icing set fully (about 2 hours for royal icing) before stacking.
recipes.storage: Store covered at room temperature up to 5 days, or refrigerate up to 10 days. Undecorated cookies or dough disks freeze up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Thumbprint Cookies
recipes.equipment: 2 baking sheets, piping bag with small round tip
recipes.chefNote: 1:1 GF baking blend with xanthan gum.

items.item: Ground cinnamon, plus more for dusting

prep: Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven; preheat to 375°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment and mist lightly with cooking spray.
method: Whisk 125g GF flour, 2g baking powder, 2.5g baking soda, 1g cinnamon, 0.5g allspice, and 1.5g salt in a medium bowl.
Whisk 107g brown sugar, 120g pumpkin puree, 75g oil, 50g egg, and 3g of the 6g vanilla in a large bowl. Add the flour mixture and gently stir with a wooden spoon until just incorporated.

Drop tablespoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart on the prepared sheets. Bake at 375°F for 6 minutes, remove, and make an indentation in the center of each with the back of a teaspoon. Return to the oven, switching pan positions, and bake 4 to 6 more minutes until set.
Cool 5 minutes on the sheets, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Beat 113g cream cheese and 28g butter until smooth. Add 60g powdered sugar, 2.5g lemon juice, the remaining 3g vanilla, and a pinch of salt; beat until incorporated. Pipe into the cooled indentations. Dust with cinnamon.
recipes.finalSeasoning: GF cookies dry out faster than wheat versions, pull them the moment the edges set rather than waiting for full color.
recipes.servingNotes: Best the day they're filled; the crumb is at its most tender.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate filled cookies up to 4 days. Unfilled cookies freeze well up to 2 months; fill after thawing.

recipes.title: Everyday Pizza Dough
recipes.equipment: Large bowl, rolling pin, pizza pan
recipes.chefNote: 1:1 GF baking blend with xanthan gum. GF dough will not pull cleanly from the bowl or stretch like wheat; press it into shape on oiled parchment, since flour makes it crack. Expect a denser, more tender crust.

items.item: Garlic powder and/or dried basil, optional
Olive oil, plus more for the bowl and finishing

method: Combine 140g of the GF flour, the yeast, 6g sugar, and 4.5g salt in a large bowl. Add garlic powder or basil here if using.
Add 28g olive oil and 175g warm water; stir well with a wooden spoon.
Gradually add the remaining 140g flour, stirring until the dough forms a cohesive, slightly sticky ball.
Oil a separate large bowl generously, transfer the dough, turning to coat, then cover tightly and set in a warm place.
Let rise 30 minutes or until noticeably puffed (GF dough won't fully double the way wheat dough does). Preheat oven to 425°F.
Turn the dough onto well-oiled parchment. Press into a 12-inch circle directly on the parchment, patching cracks with wet fingers.
Transfer parchment and all onto a pizza pan, brush the surface with a little more olive oil, and dock all over with a fork.
Add toppings and bake 13 to 15 minutes, until the crust is golden and toppings are bubbling. Slice and serve.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Not applicable, season toppings to taste.
recipes.servingNotes: Slice immediately; GF crust firms up as it sits.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Par-baked crusts (bake 6 to 7 minutes without toppings) freeze well up to 1 month, thaw and top before finishing.

recipes.title: Family Flour Tortillas
recipes.equipment: Rolling pin, medium skillet
recipes.chefNote: 1:1 GF baking blend with xanthan gum, plus psyllium husk for pliability. Without it GF tortillas crack when folded. Roll between parchment, since the dough sticks more than wheat, and knead only briefly since there is no gluten to develop.
method: Whisk 375g GF flour, 6g psyllium husk, 14g baking powder, and 10g salt together in a bowl.
Heat 240g water with 113g butter until the butter melts.
Pour the warm butter-water into the dry mixture and stir to combine.
Knead gently until the dough forms a smooth ball. Cover and rest 10 to 15 minutes.
Divide into golf-ball-sized pieces and roll each between sheets of parchment or plastic into thin rounds.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook each tortilla 30 to 45 seconds per side, until it starts to bubble and gets light brown spots.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Not applicable.
recipes.servingNotes: Serve warm, wrapped in a towel to stay pliable.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in a sealed bag up to 4 days, or freeze between parchment sheets up to 2 months. Reheat briefly in a dry skillet.

recipes.title: Basic Sourdough Loaf
recipes.timing: 20 min active / several hours (bulk ferment + proof)
recipes.equipment: Dutch oven with lid, digital scale, instant-read thermometer, banneton or towel-lined bowl
recipes.chefNote: Non-GF exception. True sourdough depends on wheat gluten for structure; a GF version needs a different starter and different hydration entirely, so it is a separate project rather than a substitution. A sluggish starter is the usual cause of a dense loaf, so wait for the float test. The Dutch oven must be fully heat-soaked, not just the oven air. Cutting hot bread gums the crumb.
prep: Feed the starter 8 to 12 hours before mixing. It is ready when it has at least doubled and floats in water.
method: Combine 500g all-purpose flour, 300g filtered water, and 115g active starter in a large bowl. Mix until no dry flour remains, then rest 45 minutes at room temperature (about 72°F) to autolyse.
Add 9g salt and squeeze it through the dough until fully incorporated, about 2 minutes. The dough will loosen, then tighten back up.

Bulk ferment 4 to 6 hours at 72°F, performing a set of stretch-and-folds every 45 minutes for the first 3 hours (4 sets total). The dough is done when it has risen about 50%, feels airy, and holds a dome rather than spreading flat.
Turn onto an unfloured counter, pre-shape into a loose round, and rest 20 minutes uncovered.
Shape tightly into a boule, seam-side up in a floured banneton. Cover and cold proof in the refrigerator 12 to 16 hours.
Place the Dutch oven with its lid on the middle rack and preheat the oven to 500°F for a full 45 minutes.
Turn the cold dough onto parchment, score 1cm deep at a shallow angle, and lower it into the hot Dutch oven. Cover and bake at 500°F for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid, drop the oven to 450°F, and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the crust is deep mahogany and the internal temperature reads 205 to 210°F.
Cool on a wire rack at least 2 hours before slicing.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Salt is fixed at 9g (1.8% of flour weight). If loaves taste flat, go to 10g rather than adding anything else.
recipes.servingNotes: Best the day it's baked, or lightly toasted after.
recipes.storage: Cut-side down on a board 2 days, or sliced and frozen up to 3 months. Refresh frozen slices straight from the freezer in a 350°F oven 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Sourdough Pizza Crust (King Arthur Style)
recipes.equipment: Pizza pan or stone
recipes.chefNote: Non-GF exception, same reasoning as the sourdough loaf.
prep: Feed the starter 8 to 12 hours ahead so it is at peak activity when you mix.
method: Mix the flour, water, starter, and salt in a large bowl until no dry flour remains. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature (about 72°F).
Knead 6 to 8 minutes by hand, until the dough passes a windowpane test and goes translucent when stretched thin without tearing.
Bulk ferment 4 to 5 hours at 72°F, until risen about 50% and visibly airy. Divide, shape into balls, and either rest 1 hour at room temperature or cold proof 12 to 24 hours for better flavor.
Place a pizza stone or steel on the upper-middle rack and preheat the oven to 500°F for 45 minutes.

Stretch each ball to a 12-inch round on a floured peel, top, and slide onto the stone. Bake at 500°F for 8 to 10 minutes, until the crust is puffed with charred blisters and the underside is set and crisp.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Not applicable.
recipes.servingNotes: Slice and serve hot.
recipes.storage: Dough balls hold refrigerated 3 days; freeze up to 1 month and thaw overnight in the fridge.

recipes.title: Overnight Sourdough Pizza Crust (Skillet Method)
recipes.timing: 20 min active / overnight ferment + 10 min cook
recipes.equipment: Cast iron skillet, broiler
recipes.chefNote: Non-GF exception, same reasoning as the sourdough loaf.
prep: Mix all dough ingredients in a large bowl until they form a shaggy mass. Cover and ferment on the counter overnight at room temperature.
The next morning, perform one set of stretches and folds, then refrigerate until ready to bake.
method: Remove dough from the fridge and let sit at room temperature 30 minutes. Divide into 4 portions, shape into balls, cover, and rest 30 minutes.
Turn the broiler to high and preheat a cast iron skillet over medium-high 5 to 6 minutes, to about 450°F surface temperature.
Press one dough ball into an 8-inch circle on a floured surface. Lay it into the hot skillet and immediately add toppings.
Cook on the stovetop 5 to 6 minutes, checking the bottom for a good char, then transfer the skillet under the broiler 2 to 4 minutes to finish the top. Slice and serve hot.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Not applicable.
recipes.servingNotes: The stovetop-to-broiler method gives a charred bottom without a pizza oven.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; dough can be cold-fermented up to 36 hours before shaping.

recipes.title: Larb Gai (Isan Minced Chicken Salad)
recipes.equipment: Wide skillet, spice grinder or food processor

items.note: uncooked Thai sticky rice, makes about double what you need here
10g in the dressing, 10g at the finish
leaves and tender stems, roughly chopped

method: Toast 40g raw glutinous rice in a dry pan over medium-low with 10g bruised lemongrass and 2g makrut lime leaf, shaking often, 8 to 12 minutes, until the grains are deep golden brown and smell like popcorn.
Cool completely, discard the lemongrass and lime leaf, and grind to a coarse sand. You need roughly 20g for this batch. Store the rest.
Warm 40g neutral oil in a saucepan or 3-quart pot over medium heat, 30 seconds. Add 150g chicken stock and bring to a simmer.

Add 900g ground turkey or chicken and break it apart into the liquid. Cover and cook over medium-low 5 to 6 minutes, stirring twice, until no pink remains and it reads 165°F internal. Pull off the heat at 165°F.
Rest off the heat, uncovered, 3 to 4 minutes. There should be 80 to 100g of liquid pooling when you tilt the pot. Never drain.
Add 60g fish sauce, 75g lime juice, 5g sugar, 5g chili flakes, and 10g toasted rice powder. Fold until evenly coated and glossy.
Fold in 90g shallots and 45g scallions.
Cool 5 minutes to just above room temperature, then fold in 25g mint, 20g cilantro, and 10g culantro.
Fold in the remaining 10g toasted rice powder just before serving.
Taste and adjust: 15g lime if flat, 10g fish sauce if it needs salt and depth, 2g chili at a time for heat.
Serve with 600g sticky rice, 200g cabbage wedges, and 150g cucumber spears.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Fish sauce and lime should land close to equal by weight, with lime slightly ahead. Adjust lime first, then fish sauce, then chili.
recipes.chefNote: Glutinous rice contains no gluten; the name refers to texture. Toasting rice powder is slow, so 40g of raw rice deliberately makes about double what one batch needs; the surplus keeps 2 to 3 months in a sealed jar. Grind it coarse. Rice powder is a sponge, so half goes in with the dressing and half at the finish, which keeps both the moisture and the nutty crunch. Standard 93 percent lean poultry carries almost no fat, so the 40g oil and 150g stock are structural, not optional. Use a saucepan rather than a wide skillet; less surface area means less evaporation. Pull at 165°F and stop, since lean poultry dries fast past that. If using 99 percent lean, add another 30g stock at step 5. The pooled liquid is part of the dressing, so never drain. Turkey runs leaner than chicken and takes an extra 10g fish sauce.
recipes.servingNotes: Eaten by hand, scooping with sticky rice and raw cabbage.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days, though the herbs dull after day one. It tightens in the fridge; loosen leftovers with 15g stock or lime juice. For freezer portions, cook and cool the plain crumbles, freeze up to 2 months, then thaw and dress fresh with new herbs.

recipes.title: Sriracha-Lime Yogurt Crema
recipes.equipment: Whisk, microplane

items.note: optional, if the sauce is too sharp

method: Zest and juice 1 lime, about 3g zest and 30g juice.
Whisk 250g Greek yogurt smooth, 20 to 30 seconds.
Whisk in 30g sriracha, 3g lime zest, and 3g kosher salt until the color is uniform pale coral with no red streaks.
Whisk in 30g lime juice in a thin stream. The sauce will loosen to drizzle consistency.
Rest 20 minutes refrigerated.
Taste and adjust: 5g honey, up to 15g more sriracha, or 1g salt at a time.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Start at 3g salt. Add honey only if it reads sharp rather than flat.
recipes.chefNote: Nonfat yogurt gives a thinner, slightly chalkier sauce but works fine. Lumps whisked in with liquid stay lumpy, hence smoothing the yogurt first. Lime juice slackens the yogurt's protein set, so add it last and stop at drizzle consistency; over-thinning only reverses with more yogurt.
