Sriracha's garlic blooms during the rest, so it tastes hotter and flatter before then. No canonical name for this one; menus call it sriracha crema.
recipes.servingNotes: Fish tacos, carnitas, grain bowls, roasted vegetables. Squeeze-bottle it for a stripe rather than a dollop.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days; it thins slightly each day. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Harissa Yogurt Sauce
recipes.equipment: Small pan, whisk, microplane

items.note: or 25g chili garlic paste, dropping the salt to 2g

method: Zest and juice 1 lemon, about 3g zest and 25g juice.
Warm 14g olive oil in a small pan over low heat, about 200°F, until it flows freely. Do not let it shimmer.
Off the heat, stir 2g garlic powder and 2g onion powder into the warm oil. Let sit 45 seconds, until they darken slightly and smell toasted.
Cool the oil mixture to room temperature, 3 to 4 minutes.
Whisk 250g Greek yogurt smooth, 20 to 30 seconds.
Whisk in 30g harissa, 3g lemon zest, and 3g kosher salt until the color is even terracotta.
Whisk in the oil mixture, then 25g lemon juice in a thin stream.
Rest 30 minutes refrigerated.
Taste and adjust: up to 10g more harissa, or 1g salt at a time.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Start at 3g salt, or 2g if using chili garlic paste, which is already salty.
recipes.chefNote: Dry alliums are dehydrated, not cooked; they need fat and gentle heat to rehydrate and lose their raw edge. Add the oil hot and it curdles the yogurt on contact. Harissa's caraway and coriander need the full rest to move through the yogurt, so this one changes more on resting than the sriracha version. Chili garlic paste substitution: 25g in place of 30g harissa, salt down to 2g.
recipes.servingNotes: General-purpose spicy yogurt sauce. Grilled meats, roasted vegetables, chickpeas, sandwiches, eggs.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Boiled Tomatillo Salsa (Salsa Verde Cocida)
recipes.equipment: Saucepan, blender
method: Husk 350g tomatillos and rinse under warm water until the skins squeak.
Combine 350g tomatillos, 350g whole roma tomatoes, 150g halved white onion, 40g whole jalapenos, and 9g garlic in a saucepan with about 1200g water, covering by 2cm.
Bring to a bare simmer over medium heat, 190 to 200°F, and hold 8 to 10 minutes. Do not let it reach a rolling boil.
Pull the pot when the tomatillos turn from bright green to dull olive and the tomato skins split.
Drain, discarding the water, and transfer everything to the blender.
Add 240g hot stock, 6g kosher salt, and 15g cilantro if using. Blend 30 to 45 seconds for smooth, or pulse 6 to 8 times for taqueria texture.
Heat 14g avocado oil to shimmering, about 350°F. Pour in the blended salsa all at once, standing back from the spatter, and fry 5 to 7 minutes until the color deepens and the raw edge cooks off.
Taste and adjust salt in 2g increments.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Start at 6g salt. Boiled salsas need more than charred ones because nothing concentrated.
recipes.chefNote: Tomatillo husks leave a bitter resin that only comes off under warm water. Hard boiling bursts the skins and floods the pot, giving a watery salsa. The olive color change beats any timer; past it the flavor flattens fast. The fry-back is optional but it is what separates a salsa from blended vegetables. Skipping it gives a brighter, greener sauce that keeps about 3 days instead of 5.
recipes.servingNotes: Loose enough to spoon over carnitas or eggs, thick enough for chips if pulsed rather than blended.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days. Freezes 3 months in 250g portions; thaw in the fridge and re-whisk.

recipes.title: Mild Salsa Roja (Tomato-Tomatillo, Boiled)
recipes.equipment: Saucepan, blender

items.note: about 2, halved, seeds and ribs removed

method: Husk 150g tomatillos and rinse under warm water until the skins squeak.
Halve 15g serranos lengthwise and scrape out the seeds and white ribs with a spoon tip.
Combine 500g whole roma tomatoes, 150g tomatillos, 100g halved white onion, 15g garlic, and the seeded serranos in a saucepan with about 1000g water, covering by 2cm.
Bring to a bare simmer at 190 to 200°F and hold 8 to 10 minutes, until the tomato skins split and the tomatillos go dull olive.
Drain, discarding the water, and transfer everything to the blender.
Add 120g hot stock and 6g kosher salt. Blend 30 to 45 seconds until smooth.
Heat 14g avocado oil to shimmering, about 350°F. Pour in the blended salsa, standing back from the spatter, and fry 5 to 7 minutes until it darkens from bright red to brick.
Taste and adjust salt in 2g increments. If it tastes flat rather than under-salted, add 5g white vinegar or lime juice.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Start at 6g salt. Flatness here is usually missing acid, not missing salt.
recipes.chefNote: The ribs carry most of the capsaicin, so scraping them is what makes this mild; seeding alone leaves the heat behind. Less stock than the verde because the tomatoes carry more body and this should coat, not run. Boiled salsas lose acid that charred ones keep, hence the vinegar correction. To raise the heat later, stir in a spoonful of the tomatillo verde. Distinct from the Charred Tomato-Guajillo Salsa Roja, which is smoky and dried-chile driven.
recipes.servingNotes: Table salsa, mild enough to pour over anything.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days. Freezes 3 months in 250g portions.

recipes.title: Savory Cottage Cheese Waffles with Broccoli
recipes.equipment: Mini waffle iron, blender or immersion blender, wire rack

items.note: full-fat or 2 percent, any curd size
leftover, finely chopped and squeezed dry

method: Chop 120g cooked broccoli into pieces no larger than 5mm. Wrap in a clean towel and squeeze hard until no more water comes out.
Blend 225g cottage cheese and 150g eggs 20 to 30 seconds, until completely smooth with no visible curd.
Whisk in 60g almond flour, 50g parmesan, 3g garlic powder, 3g onion powder, 5g everything bagel seasoning, and 2g kosher salt until no dry pockets remain.
Rest the batter 5 minutes. It will thicken to the consistency of loose pancake batter.
Fold in the squeezed 120g broccoli and 40g cheddar.
Preheat the mini waffle iron a full 5 minutes, until the indicator cycles. Brush both plates with 10g neutral oil.
Add about 55g batter per waffle, spreading to the edges. Close and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the steam slows to a wisp and the waffle is deep golden brown.
Move to a wire rack, not a plate, and rest 2 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining batter, re-oiling the plates every other waffle.
Finish with 3g everything bagel seasoning across the tops.
recipes.finalSeasoning: Everything bagel seasoning is salty, so 2g kosher salt in the batter is the ceiling. Salt the tops with seasoning, not more salt.
recipes.chefNote: Blending the cottage cheese smooth is what turns it into structure instead of wet pockets that steam the waffle from the inside. Almond flour has no gluten, so the eggs and melted cheese do all the binding, which is why the batter needs the 5 minute rest to hydrate before it will hold a shape. Wet broccoli is the main failure point; squeeze it harder than feels necessary. Do not open the iron before 4 minutes, since a cheese batter needs the full time to set and will tear. Cooling on a rack rather than a plate keeps the underside crisp.
recipes.servingNotes: Good with a fried egg, sour cream, or the sriracha-lime crema.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days, freeze up to 2 months in a single layer. Reheat straight from frozen in a toaster or a 375°F oven for 5 minutes; the microwave turns them limp.
